message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
(If you’re actually looking for an AWS EC2 instance, let me know – the syntax would be different.)

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g. us-central1-a)
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Pick a machine type that can host the GPU
#    n1-standard-8 gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"

# 3. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=${MACHINE_TYPE} \
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: your init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The GCP zone where the VM will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the official name for the RTX A6000 on GCP. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 200 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` means the VM will be stopped if the host machine is taken down for maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes. |

> **Important:**  
> * Make sure the **Compute Engine API** is enabled for your project.  
> * You’ll need a **GPU quota** for the selected zone.  
> * Billing must be enabled; GPUs incur extra charges.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (for programmatic use)

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-8"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual values.  
The `acceleratorType` field uses the same canonical name (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`) that the CLI uses.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | **GPU quota** for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in the chosen zone |
| ✅ | **Billing** enabled |
| ✅ | **Compute Engine API** enabled |
| ✅ | **Access token** (OAuth 2.0) for REST call |
| ✅ | **Firewall rules** if you need inbound traffic (e.g., SSH, HTTP) |

---

### Gotchas & Tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **“GPU type not found”** | Verify the accelerator type spelling (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). If it still fails, the zone may not support that GPU yet. Check the [GPU availability page](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#available_gpus). |
| **Quota exceeded** | Request a quota increase via the GCP console → IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| **Billing error** | Ensure your billing account is attached to the project. |
| **Image not found** | Use `--image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts` and `--image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud`. |

---

That’s all you need to launch a GPU‑enabled VM with Ubuntu 20.04 on Google Cloud. Let me know if you’d like a script that automates the quota check, or if you need help with the startup script to install CUDA, drivers, or any other software. Happy computing!
